Pándurang Pandit then marched upon Áhmedábád, and encamping near the Kankaria Lake laid siege to the city which was defended by Jawán Mard Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: About this time the _____ released Dámáji Gáikwár on his promise to help the Peshwa's brother Raghunáthráv, who was shortly afterwards despatched with an army to complete the conquest of Gujarát
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time the Peshwa released Dámáji Gáikwár on his promise to help the Peshwa's brother Raghunáthráv, who was shortly afterwards despatched with an army to complete the conquest of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, Jawán _____án's anxiety regarding the Maráthás was for a time removed by the departure of Pándurang Pandit
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: These Jawán Mard Khán accepted, and on receiving from Jawán Mard Khán the present of a mare and a small sum of money under the name of entertainment, the Marátha leader withdrew to Sorath. Meanwhile, Jawán Mard Khán's anxiety regarding the Maráthás was for a time removed by the departure of Pándurang Pandit.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Jawán _____án then marched from the city, levying tribute until he arrived on the Pálanpur frontier about seventy-five miles north of Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Certain well informed persons, who had heard of Raghunáthráv's preparations for invading Gujarát, begged Jawán Mard Khán not to leave the city but to depute his brother Zoráwar Khán Bábi to collect the tribute. Jawán Mard Khán, not believing their reports, said that he would not go more than from forty-five to sixty miles from the city, and that, should the necessity of any more distant excursion arise, he would entrust it to his brother.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Here meeting Muhammad Bahádur Jhálori, the governor of Palanpur, Jawán Mard Khán was foolishly induced to join him in plundering the fertile districts of Sirohi, till at last he was not less than ____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Here meeting Muhammad Bahádur Jhálori, the governor of Palanpur, Jawán Mard Khán was foolishly induced to join him in plundering the fertile districts of Sirohi, till at last he was not less than 150 miles from his headquarters.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, _____áthráv, joining Dámáji Gáikwár, entered suddenly by an unusual route into Gujarát, and news reached Áhmedábád that the Maráthás had crossed the Narmada River
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Meanwhile, Raghunáthráv, joining Dámáji Gáikwár, entered suddenly by an unusual route into Gujarát, and news reached Áhmedábád that the Maráthás had crossed the Narmada River. Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance co.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Kosáji, proprietor of _____, at Dámáji Gáikwár's invitation also marched towards Áhmedábád, plundering Mehmúdábád Khokhri, only three miles from the city
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Kosáji, proprietor of Nadiad, at Dámáji Gáikwár's invitation also marched towards Áhmedábád, plundering Mehmúdábád Khokhri, only three miles from the city.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In the meantime _____ reached Kaira (Kheda), and taking with him the chief man of that place, Muhammad Daurán, son of Muhammad Bábi, continued his march
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance corps under Vithal Sukhdev. In the meantime Vithal Sukhdev reached Kaira (Kheda), and taking with him the chief man of that place, Muhammad Daurán, son of Muhammad Bábi, continued his march.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was shortly joined by _____áthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance corps under Vithal Sukhdev. He was shortly joined by Raghunáthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Next day _____áthráv moved his camp to near the tomb of Sháh Bhíkan, on the bank of the Sabarmati River to the south-west of the city
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was shortly joined by Raghunáthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake. Next day Raghunáthráv moved his camp to near the tomb of Sháh Bhíkan, on the bank of the Sabarmati River to the south-west of the city.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán _____án had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán Mard Khán had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him. One of the later messengers, Mándan by name, who had not left Áhmedábád until the arrival of Raghunáthráv at the Kánkaria lake, made his way to Váv and Tharád, and told Jawán Mard Khán what had happened.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: The presence of Jawán _____án raised the spirits of the besieged, and the defence was conducted with ardour
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán Mard Khán had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him. One of the later messengers, Mándan by name, who had not left Áhmedábád until the arrival of Raghunáthráv at the Kánkaria lake, made his way to Váv and Tharád, and told Jawán Mard Khán what had happened.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At length, embarrassed by want of provisions and the clamour of his troops for pay, he extorted _____ 50,000 from the official classes
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At length, embarrassed by want of provisions and the clamour of his troops for pay, he extorted Rupees 50,000 from the official classes.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At last to _____áthráv's relief, Jawán Mard Khán was reduced to treat for peace through Vithal Sukhdev
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The official classes who were the repository of all real power murmured against his rule and openly advocated the surrender of the city, and Jawán Mard Khán, much against his will, was forced to enter into negotiations with Raghunáthráv. Raghunáthráv was so little hopeful of taking Áhmedábád that he had determined, should the siege last a month longer, to depart on condition of receiving the one-fourth share of the revenue and a safe conduct.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: It was arranged that the Maráthás should give Jawán _____án the sum of Rupees 1 lákh to pay his troops, besides presenting him with an elephant and other articles of value
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Had Jawán Mard Khán only disbursed his own money to pay the troops, and encouraged instead of disheartening the official class, he need never have lost the city. At last to Raghunáthráv's relief, Jawán Mard Khán was reduced to treat for peace through Vithal Sukhdev.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: It was further agreed that one of Jawán _____án's brothers should always serve the Maráthás with 300 horse and 500 foot, the expenses of the force being paid by the Maráthás
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: It was arranged that the Maráthás should give Jawán Mard Khán the sum of Rupees 1 lákh to pay his troops, besides presenting him with an elephant and other articles of value. And that, for himself and his brothers, Jawán Mard Khán should receive, free from any Marátha claim, the districts of Patan, Vadnagar, Sami, Munjpur, Visnagar, Tharád, Kheralu, and Rádhanpur with Tervada and Vijapur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April 1753.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: On leaving Áhmedábád Jawán _____án retired to Pátan
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April 1753. On leaving Áhmedábád Jawán Mard Khán retired to Pátan.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Áhmedábád _____áthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: This agreement was signed and sealed by Raghunáthráv, with Dámáji Gáikwár (half sharer), Malhárráv Holkar, Jye Ápa Sindhia, Rámchandar Vithal Sukhdev, Sakhárám Bhagvant, and Mádhavráv Gopálráv as securities. At Áhmedábád Raghunáthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He then marched into _____ to levy tribute from the Limbdi and Wadhwan chiefs; and was so far successful that Harbhamji of Limbḍi agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rupees 40,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He then marched into Jhalawad to levy tribute from the Limbdi and Wadhwan chiefs; and was so far successful that Harbhamji of Limbḍi agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rupees 40,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while _____ forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while Patel Vithal Sukhdev forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: From Dholka, _____áthráv went to Tárápur, about twelve miles north of Cambay (Khambhat), and compelled Momín Khán to submit to an annual payment of Rupees 10,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Áhmedábád Raghunáthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy. As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while Patel Vithal Sukhdev forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Dámáji Gáikwár, after levying tribute in the Vátrak Kántha, went to _____, which he took from Sher Khán Bábi
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Dámáji Gáikwár, after levying tribute in the Vátrak Kántha, went to Kapadvanj, which he took from Sher Khán Bábi. From Kapadvanj he passed to Naḍiád and appointed Shevakrái to collect his half share of the revenue of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: From Kapadvanj he passed to Naḍiád and appointed _____ái to collect his half share of the revenue of Gujarát
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: From Kapadvanj he passed to Naḍiád and appointed Shevakrái to collect his half share of the revenue of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Though the imperial power was sunk so low, the emperor was allowed to confer the post of Kázi of the city on Kázi Rûkn-ul-_____án who arrived at Áhmedábád and assumed office
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Though the imperial power was sunk so low, the emperor was allowed to confer the post of Kázi of the city on Kázi Rûkn-ul-Hak Khán who arrived at Áhmedábád and assumed office.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Failure of an Attempt on Cambay, _____ At the close of the year Shripatráv, who was anxious to acquire Cambay, marched against Momín Khán
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Failure of an Attempt on Cambay, 1753 At the close of the year Shripatráv, who was anxious to acquire Cambay, marched against Momín Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: After two doubtful battles in which the Maráthás gained no advantage, it was agreed that Momín Khán should pay a sum of Rupees 7000, and Shripatráv departed from Áhmedábád early in _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After the rains were over (1754) Shetuji, commander of the Áhmedábád garrison, and Shankarji, governor of Víramgám, were sent to collect tribute from Sorath. After two doubtful battles in which the Maráthás gained no advantage, it was agreed that Momín Khán should pay a sum of Rupees 7000, and Shripatráv departed from Áhmedábád early in 1754.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: When the Kolis heard of the ill success of the Maráthás at _____, they revolted and Rághoshankar was sent to subdue them
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Failure of an Attempt on Cambay, 1753 At the close of the year Shripatráv, who was anxious to acquire Cambay, marched against Momín Khán. When the Kolis heard of the ill success of the Maráthás at Cambay, they revolted and Rághoshankar was sent to subdue them.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In an engagement near Luhára in _____ in the Gáikwár's territory about eighteen miles east of Áhmedábád, Rághoshankar scattered the Kolis, but they again collected and forced the Maráthás to retire
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: In an engagement near Luhára in Bahyal in the Gáikwár's territory about eighteen miles east of Áhmedábád, Rághoshankar scattered the Kolis, but they again collected and forced the Maráthás to retire.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At this time _____ and Shankarji returned from Sorath, where they had performed the pilgrimage to Dwarka
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At this time Shetuji and Shankarji returned from Sorath, where they had performed the pilgrimage to Dwarka. Shetuji was sent to the Bhíl district against the Kolis.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Shetuji was sent to the Bhíl district against the _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: When the Kolis heard of the ill success of the Maráthás at Cambay, they revolted and Rághoshankar was sent to subdue them. In an engagement near Luhára in Bahyal in the Gáikwár's territory about eighteen miles east of Áhmedábád, Rághoshankar scattered the Kolis, but they again collected and forced the Maráthás to retire.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was unsuccessful, and was so ashamed of his failure that he returned to the _____ and Dandu Dátátri was appointed in his place
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was unsuccessful, and was so ashamed of his failure that he returned to the Dakhan and Dandu Dátátri was appointed in his place.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In this year died Nek Álam Khán II, governor of _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: In this year died Nek Álam Khán II, governor of Broach.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was succeeded by his brother _____án who expelled his nephew Hámid Beg, son of Nek Álam Khán
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was succeeded by his brother Khertalab Khán who expelled his nephew Hámid Beg, son of Nek Álam Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Hámid Beg took refuge in _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Hámid Beg took refuge in Surat.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Bálásinor a dispute arose between _____án Bábi and a body of Arab mercenaries who took possession of a hill, but in the end came to terms
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Bálásinor a dispute arose between Sher Khán Bábi and a body of Arab mercenaries who took possession of a hill, but in the end came to terms.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Maráthás Attack Cambay, _____ With the Peshwa's permission his deputy Bhagvantráv marched on Cambay
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Maráthás Attack Cambay, 1754 With the Peshwa's permission his deputy Bhagvantráv marched on Cambay.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Subsequently, a letter from _____áv to Sálim Jamádár at Áhmedábád ordering him to march against Cambay fell into Momín Khán's hands
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Maráthás Attack Cambay, 1754 With the Peshwa's permission his deputy Bhagvantráv marched on Cambay. When Bhagvantráv arrived at Cambay he showed no hostile intentions and was well received by Momín Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He at once surrounded _____áv's house and made him prisoner
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: When Bhagvantráv arrived at Cambay he showed no hostile intentions and was well received by Momín Khán. Subsequently, a letter from Bhagvantráv to Sálim Jamádár at Áhmedábád ordering him to march against Cambay fell into Momín Khán's hands.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: When the Peshwa heard that _____áv had been captured, he ordered Ganesh Ápa, governor of Jambusar, as well as the governors of Víramgám, Dhandhuka, and other places to march at once upon Cambay
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: When Bhagvantráv arrived at Cambay he showed no hostile intentions and was well received by Momín Khán. Subsequently, a letter from Bhagvantráv to Sálim Jamádár at Áhmedábád ordering him to march against Cambay fell into Momín Khán's hands.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Shortly afterwards _____áv was recalled by the Peshwa and his place supplied by an officer of the name of Rágho
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Eventually Shripatráv, the Peshwa's deputy, sent the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi to negotiate, and it was agreed that Bhagvantráv should be released and that no alteration should be made in the position of Momín Khán. Shortly afterwards Shripatráv was recalled by the Peshwa and his place supplied by an officer of the name of Rágho.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: About this time _____án, governor of Broach, died, and quarrels arose regarding the succession
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time Khertalab Khán, governor of Broach, died, and quarrels arose regarding the succession. Ultimately Hamid Beg, nephew of Khertalab Khán, obtained the post, and he afterwards received an imperial order confirming him as governor, and bestowing on him the title of Neknám Khán Bahádur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Ultimately Hamid Beg, nephew of _____án, obtained the post, and he afterwards received an imperial order confirming him as governor, and bestowing on him the title of Neknám Khán Bahádur
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time Khertalab Khán, governor of Broach, died, and quarrels arose regarding the succession. Ultimately Hamid Beg, nephew of Khertalab Khán, obtained the post, and he afterwards received an imperial order confirming him as governor, and bestowing on him the title of Neknám Khán Bahádur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Delhi, during _____, the emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur was deposed, and Âzíz-ud-dín, son of Jahándár Sháh, was raised to the throne with the title of Alamgir II
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Delhi, during 1754, the emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur was deposed, and Âzíz-ud-dín, son of Jahándár Sháh, was raised to the throne with the title of Alamgir II.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: The chief _____ houses, Gaikwar and Peshwa had made peace with each other and driven out the Mughal nobles under the emperor Alamgir II
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: The Mughal Empire's province Gujarat (now in India) was under attack of the Marathas since last half century. The chief Maratha houses, Gaikwar and Peshwa had made peace with each other and driven out the Mughal nobles under the emperor Alamgir II.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: One such noble, Momin Khan, had countered their advances and recovered Ahmedabad in _____ lost to the Marathas few years ago
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: One such noble, Momin Khan, had countered their advances and recovered Ahmedabad in 1756 lost to the Marathas few years ago.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: After a long siege, _____ fell again in hands of the Marathas
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: One such noble, Momin Khan, had countered their advances and recovered Ahmedabad in 1756 lost to the Marathas few years ago. After a long siege, Ahmedabad fell again in hands of the Marathas.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: In _____, the English of the British East India Company captured Surat
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: In 1759, the English of the British East India Company captured Surat.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: Sadashiv Ramchandra was appointed as a viceroy by Peshwa in _____ followed by Apa Ganesh in 1761
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: Sadashiv Ramchandra was appointed as a viceroy by Peshwa in 1760 followed by Apa Ganesh in 1761.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: Thus the _____ firmly established themselves in Gujarat
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: Following defeat of Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), the nobles briefly recovered towns from the Marathas but soon had to surrender. Thus the Marathas firmly set up themselves in Gujarat.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: Maratha leader _____áv who was held captive was released and he established himself in the Cambay fort of Nápád and not long after began to attack Mughal noble Momín Khán's villages
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: Maratha leader Bhagvantráv who was held captive was released and he set up himself in the Cambay fort of Nápád and not long after began to attack Mughal noble Momín Khán's villages. This arrangement was made through the mediation of Tukáji, the steward of Sadáshiv Dámodar, who had come to Gujarát with an army and orders to help Bhagvantráv.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: This arrangement was made through the mediation of Tukáji, the steward of Sadáshiv Dámodar, who had come to Gujarát with an army and orders to help _____áv
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: Maratha leader Bhagvantráv who was held captive was released and he set up himself in the Cambay fort of Nápád and not long after began to attack Mughal noble Momín Khán's villages. This arrangement was made through the mediation of Tukáji, the steward of Sadáshiv Dámodar, who had come to Gujarát with an army and orders to help Bhagvantráv.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: Contest with Momín Khán Renewed, _____ After several doubtful engagements peace was concluded on Momín Khán paying Rupees 10,000 on account of the usual share of the Maráthás which he had withheld
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: Contest with Momín Khán Renewed, 1754 After several doubtful engagements peace was concluded on Momín Khán paying Rupees 10,000 on account of the usual share of the Maráthás which he had withheld.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: As he was not in a position to meet their demands he sent a body of men against some villages to the west belonging to _____ and plundered them, dividing the booty among his troops
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: As he was not in a position to meet their demands he sent a body of men against some villages to the west belonging to Limbdi and plundered them, dividing the booty among his troops.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: In the following year, _____, Momín Khán went to Ghogha, a port which, though at one time subordinate to Cambay (Khambhat), had fallen into the hands of Sher Khán Bábi, and was now in the possession o
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: In the following year, 1755, Momín Khán went to Ghogha, a port which, though at one time subordinate to Cambay (Khambhat), had fallen into the hands of Sher Khán Bábi, and was now in the possession of the Peshwa's officers.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: Ghogha fell and leaving a garrison of 100 Arabs under Ibráhím Kúli Khán, Momín Khán returned to _____, levying tribute
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: In the following year, 1755, Momín Khán went to Ghogha, a port which, though at one time subordinate to Cambay (Khambhat), had fallen into the hands of Sher Khán Bábi, and was now in the possession of the Peshwa's officers. Ghogha fell and leaving a garrison of 100 Arabs under Ibráhím Kúli Khán, Momín Khán returned to Cambay, levying tribute.

Gujarat under Alamgir II.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Alamgir II.question: Here they remained until their arrears were paid off, and then returned to _____
Gujarat under Alamgir II.fact: In the following year, 1755, Momín Khán went to Ghogha, a port which, though at one time subordinate to Cambay (Khambhat), had fallen into the hands of Sher Khán Bábi, and was now in the possession of the Peshwa's officers. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán next interfered with the lands of _____án Bábi, the deputy governor of Godhra, and his brothers
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán next interfered with the lands of Safdar Khán Bábi, the deputy governor of Godhra, and his brothers.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On one of the brothers repairing to Delhi and remonstrating, _____ Kúli, restored their lands to the Bábis
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In consequence of the enmity between Haidar Kúli Khán and the Márwáris, Shujáât Khán, the deputy viceroy, attacked the house of Náhir Khán who had been Ajítsingh's minister, and forced him to pay Rupees 100000 and leave the city. On one of the brothers repairing to Delhi and remonstrating, Haidar Kúli, restored their lands to the Bábis.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shortly after one of the viceroy's officers, Kásím Áli Khán, while employed against the Kolis of that part of the country, was killed at _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly after one of the viceroy's officers, Kásím Áli Khán, while employed against the Kolis of that part of the country, was killed at Pethapur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Next, he passed into _____, and after exacting tribute, crossed to Kutch
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Next, he passed into Sorath, and after exacting tribute, crossed to Kutch. In 1721, a Sayad was sent to Sorath as deputy governor in place of Muhammad Sharíf, and Haidar Kúli was appointed governor of Kadi, the Chúnvál, and Halvad (called Muhammadnagar), and put in charge of Tharad, Arjanpur, Bhámnárli, Pethápur, and Kheralu in place of Vakhatsingh, son of the Mahárája Ajítsingh.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The chief opposed him, and in the fight that followed was beaten and forced to pay about _____ 225000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The chief opposed him, and in the fight that followed was beaten and forced to pay about Rupees 225000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Early in _____, Nizám-ul-Mulk took up the office of prime minister of the empire, to which he had been appointed in the previous year
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Early in 1722, Nizám-ul-Mulk took up the office of prime minister of the empire, to which he had been appointed in the previous year.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Haidar Kúli Khán, unable to contend with the Nizám, left _____ and retired to Gujarát
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Strenuous efforts were made to embroil him with Haidar Kúli Khán, as the Nizám's austerity and craft were a source of not less anxiety to the Dehli court than Haidar Kúli's more daring and restless ambition. Haidar Kúli Khán, unable to contend with the Nizám, left Dehli and retired to Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On his way the villagers of Dabháli opposed him killing one of his chief men named _____án
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On his way the villagers of Dabháli opposed him killing one of his chief men named Alif Beg Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time, among other changes, _____ádúr, son of Salábat Khán Bábi, was placed in charge of Sádra and Virpur, with the title of Sher Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time, among other changes, Muhammad Bahádúr, son of Salábat Khán Bábi, was placed in charge of Sádra and Virpur, with the title of Sher Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shortly after his arrival the viceroy marched against and subdued the rebellious Kolis of the Chunvál, appointing _____ Áli Khán his governor there
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly after his arrival the viceroy marched against and subdued the rebellious Kolis of the Chunvál, appointing Rustam Áli Khán his governor there.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Then, returning to Áhmedábád, he took up his residence in the _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Then, returning to Áhmedábád, he took up his residence in the Bhadra.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shows signs of Independence and is Recalled, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shows signs of Independence and is Recalled, 1722.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time _____ Kúli aimed at bringing all Gujarát under his rule
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Haidar Kúli aimed at bringing all Gujarát under his rule.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He seized the imperial horses which passed through Áhmedábád on their way to _____, and confiscated many estates and gave them to his own men
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He seized the imperial horses which passed through Áhmedábád on their way to Delhi, and confiscated many estates and gave them to his own men.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On his way to enforce tribute from the _____úr chiefs, he levied Rupees 80,000 from Lunavada
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On his way to enforce tribute from the Dungarpúr chiefs, he levied Rupees 80,000 from Lunavada. Through the mediation of the Udaipur Rána, and as he agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 100000, the Rával of Dungarpur escaped.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Through the mediation of the _____ Rána, and as he agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 100000, the Rával of Dungarpur escaped
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Through the mediation of the Udaipur Rána, and as he agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 100000, the Rával of Dungarpur escaped.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Haidar Kúli Khán, finding himself no match for the Nizám, was induced to retire quietly, and accordingly left Gujarát by way of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Through the mediation of the Udaipur Rána, and as he agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 100000, the Rával of Dungarpur escaped. Haidar Kúli Khán, finding himself no match for the Nizám, was induced to retire quietly, and accordingly left Gujarát by way of Dungarpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán and _____ Áli Khán accompanied him as far as Dungarpúr, and then returned to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán and Rustam Áli Khán accompanied him as far as Dungarpúr, and then returned to Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Subsequently, the Nizám came to _____át and chose officers of his own for places of trust, the chief of whom was Momín Khán, who was appointed governor of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Haidar Kúli Khán, finding himself no match for the Nizám, was induced to retire quietly, and accordingly left Gujarát by way of Dungarpur. Subsequently, the Nizám came to Gujarát and chose officers of his own for places of trust, the chief of whom was Momín Khán, who was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, in _____át dissensions sprang up between Hámid Khán and other officers, but matters were arranged without any outbreak of hostility
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Subsequently, the Nizám came to Gujarát and chose officers of his own for places of trust, the chief of whom was Momín Khán, who was appointed governor of Surat. Meanwhile, in Gujarát dissensions sprang up between Hámid Khán and other officers, but matters were arranged without any outbreak of hostility.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Tribute was exacted from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river and from _____ an unruly Koli village was burned down, and garrisons were placed in the Koli country
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Tribute was exacted from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river and from Modhera an unruly Koli village was burned down, and garrisons were placed in the Koli country.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____ Rustam Áli Khán and Shujáât Khán were ordered from Delhi to march on Jodhpur, which they captured and plundered, and then returned to Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1723 Rustam Áli Khán and Shujáât Khán were ordered from Delhi to march on Jodhpur, which they captured and plundered, and then returned to Áhmedábád. Marathas return In 1723, Piláji Gáikwár, who had been long hovering on the frontier, marched on Surat and was opposed by Momín Khán, whom he defeated.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Marathas return In _____, Piláji Gáikwár, who had been long hovering on the frontier, marched on Surat and was opposed by Momín Khán, whom he defeated
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1723 Rustam Áli Khán and Shujáât Khán were ordered from Delhi to march on Jodhpur, which they captured and plundered, and then returned to Áhmedábád. Marathas return In 1723, Piláji Gáikwár, who had been long hovering on the frontier, marched on Surat and was opposed by Momín Khán, whom he defeated.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At the same time Kántáji _____ Bánde, invading Gujarát from the side of Dahod, began to levy fixed contributions
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At the same time Kántáji Kadam Bánde, invading Gujarát from the side of Dahod, began to levy fixed contributions.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Though before this occasional demands had often been made, _____ was the first year in which the Maráthás imposed a regular tribute on Gujarát
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Marathas return In 1723, Piláji Gáikwár, who had been long hovering on the frontier, marched on Surat and was opposed by Momín Khán, whom he defeated. Though before this occasional demands had often been made, 1723 was the first year in which the Maráthás imposed a regular tribute on Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Momín Khán was now appointed provincial minister, and _____ Áli Khán succeeded him as revenue officer of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Momín Khán was now appointed provincial minister, and Rustam Áli Khán succeeded him as revenue officer of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He selected _____áât Khán as his deputy, and made other arrangements for the government of the province
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He selected Shujáât Khán as his deputy, and made other arrangements for the government of the province. Hámid Khán, uncle and deputy of the Nizám, prepared to oppose Shujáât Khán, but through the intervention of Bábis Salábat Khán, Safdar Khán, and Jawán Mard Khán, Hámid Khán evacuated the Bhadra, and withdrew to Dahod.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán now went to collect tribute, leaving Ibráhím Kúli Khán at Áhmedábád, while Rámrái was posted at _____ in Kaira, with orders to watch the movements of Hámid Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán now went to collect tribute, leaving Ibráhím Kúli Khán at Áhmedábád, while Rámrái was posted at Mahudha in Kaira, with orders to watch the movements of Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As the viceroy was in need of money, he farmed to one Jívan Jugal the districts of _____, Makbúlábad or Amod about twenty-two miles north of Bharuch, Dholka, and Bharuch
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: As the viceroy was in need of money, he farmed to one Jívan Jugal the districts of Jambusar, Makbúlábad or Amod about twenty-two miles north of Bharuch, Dholka, and Bharuch.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____, he came to Áhmedábád with Áli Muhammad Khán father of the author of the Mirát-i-Áhmedi, as his private minister
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1724, he came to Áhmedábád with Áli Muhammad Khán father of the author of the Mirát-i-Áhmedi, as his private minister.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The emperor accepted this offer, allowing _____ Áli to draw on the Surat treasury to the extent of Rupees 200000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rustam Áli, governor of Surat, having succeeded twice or thrice in defeating the Maráthás under Píláji Gáikwár, now offered, in conjunction with his brother Shujáât Khán, that if 20,000 men were placed under their orders, they would march against the Nizám. The emperor accepted this offer, allowing Rustam Áli to draw on the Surat treasury to the extent of Rupees 200000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He promised to Kántáji _____ Bánde a one-fourth share of the revenue of Gujarát, provided he should be able, in concert with Hámid Khán, to re-conquer the province from Mubáriz-ul-Mulk
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He promised to Kántáji Kadam Bánde a one-fourth share of the revenue of Gujarát, provided he should be able, in concert with Hámid Khán, to re-conquer the province from Mubáriz-ul-Mulk. Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán, who was now at Kadi, instead of following the advice of his minister and carefully watching Hámid Khán's movements from _____, went to a distant part of the province
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán, who was now at Kadi, instead of following the advice of his minister and carefully watching Hámid Khán's movements from Kapadvanj, went to a distant part of the province. Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán, who was now at Kadi, instead of following the advice of his minister and carefully watching Hámid Khán's movements from Kapadvanj, went to a distant part of the province. Hámid Khán seeing his opportunity, united his forces with those of Kántáji Kadam, and marched to Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán hearing of this, advanced towards Áhmedábád and encamped at _____ near Áhmedábád and then proceeded to Mota Medra, about six miles east of the capital
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán hearing of this, advanced towards Áhmedábád and encamped at Dabhoda near Áhmedábád and then proceeded to Mota Medra, about six miles east of the capital.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán seeing that _____áât Khán had but a small force, marched between him and the capital
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán hearing of this, advanced towards Áhmedábád and encamped at Dabhoda near Áhmedábád and then proceeded to Mota Medra, about six miles east of the capital. Hámid Khán seeing that Shujáât Khán had but a small force, marched between him and the capital.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: A battle was fought, in which Shujáât Khán was slain, and his two sons Hasan Kúli and _____ Kúli were taken prisoners
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: A battle was fought, in which Shujáât Khán was slain, and his two sons Hasan Kúli and Mustafa Kúli were taken prisoners.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to _____án Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to Safdar Khán Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán now sent a message to the emperor, that the Maráthás had been successful in defeating _____áât Khán and conquering Gujarát, but that he had defended Áhmedábád against them
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: A battle was fought, in which Shujáât Khán was slain, and his two sons Hasan Kúli and Mustafa Kúli were taken prisoners. Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to Safdar Khán Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji went to _____ and besieged the town, but on the promise of one of the chief inhabitants to raise a sum of Rupees 350000, the Maráthás retired
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kántáji went to Viramgam and besieged the town, but on the promise of one of the chief inhabitants to raise a sum of Rupees 350000, the Maráthás retired.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Ibráhím Kúli, son of _____áât Khán, in revenge for his father's death, determined to assassinate Hámid Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ibráhím Kúli, son of Shujáât Khán, in revenge for his father's death, determined to assassinate Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji promised to aid _____án, and the allied armies, crossing the Mahi River, encamped at Aras in the plain between Anand Anand and the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Píláji promised to aid Rustam Khán, and the allied armies, crossing the Mahi River, encamped at Aras in the plain between Anand Anand and the Mahi. Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, _____ábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: A battle was fought, in which, though Piláji took no part, Hámid Khán was defeated and put to flight, and Mír _____ was killed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán. A battle was fought, in which, though Piláji took no part, Hámid Khán was defeated and put to flight, and Mír Nathu was killed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: After the fight _____ Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, Muhammad Salábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán. After the fight Rustam Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji plundered _____ Áli's camp and then moved off, while Kántáji carried away what was left in the camp of Hámid Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: After the fight Rustam Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp. Píláji plundered Rustam Áli's camp and then moved off, while Kántáji carried away what was left in the camp of Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Now, as the Maráthás really desired to ruin _____ Áli, who was their bitter foe, they after a few days surrounded him and cut off his supplies
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: After the fight Rustam Áli remained on the field of battle and liberated his nephews, plundering Hámid Khán's camp. Píláji plundered Rustam Áli's camp and then moved off, while Kántáji carried away what was left in the camp of Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán reproached Kántáji for his inactivity; but he pleaded in excuse that he was watching the mode of warfare amongst _____, and promised to attack Rustam Áli shortly
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Hámid Khán reproached Kántáji for his inactivity; but he pleaded in excuse that he was watching the mode of warfare amongst Mughals, and promised to attack Rustam Áli shortly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He extorted large sums from the rich, and poisoned the two sons of _____áât Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He extorted large sums from the rich, and poisoned the two sons of Shujáât Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the news of Kántáji's and Píláji's success reached the Dakhan, _____, son of Khanderáv Senápati, came with a large army and laid siege to Cambay
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When the news of Kántáji's and Píláji's success reached the Dakhan, Trimbak Rao Dabhade, son of Khanderáv Senápati, came with a large army and laid siege to Cambay.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk recaptures the province from Hamid Khan and the Maráthás, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk recaptures the province from Hamid Khan and the Maráthás, 1725.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Salábat Khán, leaving Áhmedábád, went to Víramgám, and after some time, placing his nephew at Víramgám, he went into _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Salábat Khán, leaving Áhmedábád, went to Víramgám, and after some time, placing his nephew at Víramgám, he went into Gohilwad.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the news of the defeat and death of _____ Áli reached Delhi, the emperor ordered Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to take a strong army and proceed in person to Gujarát and expel Hámid Khán and the Maráthás
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When the news of the defeat and death of Rustam Áli reached Delhi, the emperor ordered Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to take a strong army and proceed in person to Gujarát and expel Hámid Khán and the Maráthás.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched on Gujarát with a large army, assisted by Mahárája _____ of Jodhpur, Chatarsingh Rája of Narwar in Bundelkhand, Gandrapsingh, and the Mahárána of Udaipur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched on Gujarát with a large army, assisted by Mahárája Abheysingh of Jodhpur, Chatarsingh Rája of Narwar in Bundelkhand, Gandrapsingh, and the Mahárána of Udaipur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At that time Salábat Khán was removed from his government, and _____án Bábi died
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At that time Salábat Khán was removed from his government, and Safdar Khán Bábi died.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In obedience to the imperial order, Mubáriz-ul-_____ marched from Ajmer and came to the Gujarát frontier
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched on Gujarát with a large army, assisted by Mahárája Abheysingh of Jodhpur, Chatarsingh Rája of Narwar in Bundelkhand, Gandrapsingh, and the Mahárána of Udaipur. On his arrival at Ajmer, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk was received by his private minister Áli Muhammad Khán, who afterwards joined Jawán Mard Khán Bábi in Rádhanpur, and united their troops with those under Mubáriz-ul-Mulk.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: He placed Rúpsingh and Sardár _____ in charge of the city and himself withdrew to Mehmúdábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He placed Rúpsingh and Sardár Muhammad Ghorni in charge of the city and himself withdrew to Mehmúdábád. When Sheikh Alíyár arrived before the city, Muhammad Ghorni, who was dissatisfied with Hámid Khán for bringing in the Maráthás, persuaded Rúpsingh to fly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk now sent _____íyár in advance with an army against Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk now sent Sheikh Alíyár in advance with an army against Áhmedábád. When Sheikh Alíyár arrived before the city, Muhammad Ghorni, who was dissatisfied with Hámid Khán for bringing in the Maráthás, persuaded Rúpsingh to fly.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In the meantime Mubáriz-ul-Mulk with the main body of his forces reached _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the meantime Mubáriz-ul-Mulk with the main body of his forces reached Sidhpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán, accompanied by a detachment of Marátha horse, now returned to Áhmedábád; but _____ closed the gates, and would not suffer him to enter the city
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When Sheikh Alíyár arrived before the city, Muhammad Ghorni, who was dissatisfied with Hámid Khán for bringing in the Maráthás, persuaded Rúpsingh to fly. Hámid Khán, accompanied by a detachment of Marátha horse, now returned to Áhmedábád; but Muhammad Ghorni closed the gates, and would not suffer him to enter the city.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk marched to Mehsana.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Áli _____án, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi.
